facts.statement: Hualianceratops was a herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur that lived approximately 160 million years ago in western China.
facts.quote: Hualianceratops is a genus of herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur that lived about 160 million years ago in the Late Jurassic epoch in what is now western China.

facts.statement: The size of Hualianceratops was compared to that of a spaniel.
facts.quote: Its size has been compared to that of a spaniel.

facts.statement: The species Hualianceratops wucaiwanensis was named and described in 2015 by Han Fenglu, Catherine A. Forster, James M. Clark, and Xu Xing.
facts.quote: In 2015, the type species Hualianceratops wucaiwanensis was named and described by Han Fenglu, Catherine A. Forster, James M. Clark, and Xu Xing.

facts.statement: The generic name Hualianceratops combines Chinese words for "ornamental face" with the Greek term for "hornface" to reference the ornamentation on its jaw bones.
facts.quote: The generic name combines the Chinese hua, "ornamental", and lian, "face", a reference to the ornamentation of the jaw bones, with ceratops, Latinised Greek for "hornface", a usual suffix in the names of ceratopsians.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil was found in the upper Shishugou Formation, which dates to the Oxfordian stage.
facts.quote: The holotype, IVPP V18641, was found in a layer of the upper Shishugou Formation dating from the Oxfordian.

facts.statement: Hualianceratops was a small genus measuring about 1.2 meters in length.
facts.quote: Hulianceratops is a small genus, about 1.2 m long.

facts.statement: The estimated skull length of Hualianceratops was 25 centimeters.
facts.quote: The skull length was estimated at 25 cm.

facts.statement: The dentary bone of the lower jaw in Hualianceratops is described as deep and short.
facts.quote: The dentary bone of the lower jaw is deep and short.

facts.statement: The maxilla of Hualianceratops bears at least nine teeth, while the dentary bears at least seven.
facts.quote: The maxilla bears at least nine teeth, the dentary at least seven.

facts.statement: In 2015, Hualianceratops was classified within the family Chaoyangsauridae.
facts.quote: In 2015, Hualianceratops was placed in the Chaoyangsauridae.

facts.statement: Hualianceratops belongs to the family Chaoyangsauridae.
The skull of Hualianceratops was 25 centimeters long.
facts.quote: El cráneo tenía 25 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: Hualianceratops had a vegetarian diet and was likely prey for the tyrannosauroid dinosaur Guanlong.
facts.quote: Era de dieta vegetariana y probablemente era presa del dinosaurio tiranosauroide Guanlong.

facts.statement: The bones of Hualianceratops were not smooth but had a texture, leading paleontologists to call it the "ornamented dinosaur".
facts.quote: Los huesos no eran lisos sino que tenían una textura, por lo que se le ha llamado "dinosaurio adornado" u "ornamentado" por sus paleontólogos descubridores.

facts.statement: As one of the oldest ceratopsians, Hualianceratops lacked the typical horns and frills seen in later specimens like Triceratops.
facts.quote: Al ser de los ceratopsianos más antiguos no muestra la típica cornamenta y volante vistos en especímenes de épocas posteriores, como el del famoso Triceratops, que vivió a fines del período Cretácico.

facts.statement: Hualianceratops lived during the Oxfordian stage, between 161.5 and 154.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Oxfordian (161.5 to 154.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: It remains unresolved how Hualianceratops relates to other members of its clade.
facts.quote: The relationships with other members of its clade could not be resolved.

rejected.statement: Hualianceratops was discovered in eastern China and measured approximately 1.5 meters in length.
rejected.quote: Fue descubierto en el este de China y su tamaño era comparable al de un perro spaniel, es decir, aproximadamente un metro y medio de largo.
